body:
Releasing the claim on the dev run's teardown. Product commit ca04ced.

The report — "After closing the app sub processes keeps running and you can't start the app again" — is one
event, not two, and it is not the sidecar.

Found live: a vite server running with no `dev.mjs` anywhere and its launching shell already gone, holding
`--strictPort` 5173. That is the whole failure. `dev.mjs` starts vite and electron and takes both down when
it stops — its own header promises "no orphan server squatting on 5173" — but only while it is alive to run
the handler. Kill the supervisor itself (a closed console, an ended session, `taskkill /F`) and both
children are orphaned, because neither Node nor Windows ties a child's lifetime to its parent. Vite then
keeps the port, so the next `npm run dev` refuses to start; Electron keeps the single-instance lock, so a
relaunch exits without drawing a window. Both read to a person as "the app is broken".

Shipped: `scripts/supervised.mjs`, which runs one command and reaps its whole tree when the pid it was
started for disappears — no cooperation needed from that supervisor, which is the point, since the failure
it covers is the supervisor not being there. It waits for its own `taskkill` rather than firing and
forgetting it, because exiting on the next tick leaves the killer as the only survivor: the same bug one
level down, and exactly what `before-quit` does today. `dev.mjs` runs both children through it.

Verified by killing things rather than reading them:
- Supervisor hard-killed with no `/T`: vite, electron, the sidecar and both wrappers gone within 4s, 5173
  free. That is precisely what leaked before the change.
- Window closed gracefully: same result — nothing left, port free.
- Start, close, start again: the reported journey, working.

Explicitly NOT changed, and this is the deliberate part: `index.ts`'s teardown. The sidecar does not leak
on this machine by any path I could construct — closing the built app is clean, hard-killing its main
process is clean (Electron on Windows keeps its children in a job object that dies with it), and killing
the sidecar's own parent takes the child with it. Rewriting the quit path on a hypothesis would be the
mistake this session made once already today and caught by measuring first. Recorded instead: the sidecar
appears as two python processes with identical command lines, unexplained and not chased.

Files touched: app/scripts/dev.mjs, app/scripts/supervised.mjs. Safe to touch both now.
